hook.text: One pawn is almost home, but Black plants a knight in the road. Can you see why the obvious finish is not so simple?

yt_detail: Anton Guijarro turns a passer into a win
title: The Pawn That Would Not Stop
description: David Anton Guijarro faces Arthur de Winter in Round 1 of the German Bundesliga 2026/27 (Schachbundesliga), played in Neuwied, Germany. This classical game starts as an English Opening and turns into a sharp queenside race. Watch for the outside passer, the material sacrifice the engine approves, and the strange final twist before the recorded 1-0 result.

segments.text: This is round one of the German Bundesliga twenty twenty-six to twenty-seven, played in Neuwied, Germany, at classical time control. David Anton Guijarro, rated two thousand six hundred fifty, has White against Arthur de Winter, rated two thousand four hundred fifty-nine. Before this game, the broadcast table already listed eight players on one point.

The position has simplified, but White is still pressing hard. The rook swings over: {{m:57}}. Black tries to distract it: {{m:58}}. White removes the pawn: {{m:59}}. Black centralizes the king: {{m:60}}.
Anton keeps the rook active: {{m:61}}. Black pushes a passer of his own: {{m:62}}. It looks like technique, but one tempo can flip the story.

White has a tempting push here. Is it safe? {{p}} In the game, White chooses: {{m:63}}. The engine suddenly swings back toward Black, and Black creates his own threat: {{m:64}}. The score ends there: de Winter resigned, so Anton Guijarro took the point. That is why this game matters: a modern Bundesliga fight where a passed pawn dominated the board, and the final position still asks questions.
